title: Testing Training and Inference Pipelines knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “Small synthetic datasets” in this lesson?
options: This topic guarantees identical results across all devices and package versions.
This topic makes every serialized checkpoint safe to load from an unknown source.
Inspect one sample before batching, verify feature/label alignment, and confirm that preprocessing and split boundaries fit the intended stage.
This topic removes the need to validate inputs or inspect model outputs.
questions.answer_key: Inspect one sample before batching, verify feature/label alignment, and confirm that preprocessing and split boundaries fit the intended stage.
questions.explanation: Small synthetic datasets: Inspect one sample before batching, verify feature/label alignment, and confirm that preprocessing and split boundaries fit the intended stage.

questions.prompt: Before relying on “Smoke tests”, what should a learner verify?
options: Skip recording package versions because they cannot affect API or device behavior.
include positive and negative cases, appropriate tolerances, gradient/shape assertions, and a documented artifact-trust policy.
Assume all tensor dimensions and devices are interchangeable without checking them.
Use the held-out test split repeatedly to tune the model and report that score as unbiased.
questions.answer_key: include positive and negative cases, appropriate tolerances, gradient/shape assertions, and a documented artifact-trust policy.
questions.explanation: This lesson recommends the following check: include positive and negative cases, appropriate tolerances, gradient/shape assertions, and a documented artifact-trust policy.

questions.prompt: Which pitfall matters when applying “End-to-end forward passes”?
options: Do not hide all exceptions or assume bitwise equality across devices and package versions.
Change several unrelated settings at once and infer which change fixed the result.
Treat successful imports as proof that the full model and evaluation pipeline are correct.
Catch every exception and silently replace failed results with zeros.
questions.answer_key: Do not hide all exceptions or assume bitwise equality across devices and package versions.
questions.explanation: This topic-specific caution is important: Do not hide all exceptions or assume bitwise equality across devices and package versions.
